title: Eagle undocking
scope: A selected Apollo 11 pre-undocking checklist and CSM release procedure. Backend-owned discrete training state; no original AGC execution, pressure model, latch dynamics, spacecraft physics or historical state vector.

historicalReference.clockMeaning: Reference labels only; player actions have no reconstructed historical GET.

entryPreconditions.label: Armstrong and Aldrin in Eagle; Collins in Columbia.
Vehicle umbilicals removed/stowed; drogue and probe installed; probe umbilicals connected and probe preloaded; twelve docking-ring latches manually released/cocked; hatch secured.
Hatch integrity check and final tunnel venting completed; tunnel valve OFF; tunnel lights OFF. No measured pressures are supplied.
Earlier LM activation, landing gear deployment, RCS/DPS checks, AGS calibration/update, undocking attitude and mission-control go/no-go are assumed completed.
Original P47/AGS undocking delta-V bookkeeping was required in the flown procedure; it is not executed by this trainer.

steps.label: Verify completed tunnel closeout
steps.instructions: Acknowledge the entry setup below. These earlier mechanical and pressure checks are assumed completed; this trainer does not simulate them.

steps.label: Report LM helmets, gloves and communications ready
steps.instructions: Both LM crew have helmets and gloves on. Verify basic voice communication and the VHF B backup. This is a crew report.

steps.label: Verify overhead hatch and cabin configuration
steps.instructions: Report hatch LOCKED, overhead relief/dump valve AUTO and regulators A/B CABIN. Mission/event timer setup is a reference, not a running historical clock.

steps.label: GUID CONT
steps.instructions: Select the abort guidance system for this pre-undocking configuration. This does not run an AGS emulator.

steps.label: Verify the pre-undocking display selections
steps.instructions: Report the ACT-62 display configuration. These monitor selections do not establish a spacecraft attitude or navigation solution.
referenceItems: RATE ERR MON CDR: LDG RDR/CMPTR; LMP: RNDZ RDR
ATTITUDE MON CDR: PGNS; LMP: AGS

steps.label: ATTITUDE CONTROL ROLL
steps.instructions: All three independent axis switches must be checked.

steps.label: ATTITUDE CONTROL PITCH
steps.instructions: All three independent axis switches must be checked.

steps.label: ATTITUDE CONTROL YAW
steps.instructions: All three independent axis switches must be checked.

steps.label: MODE CONT PGNS
steps.instructions: The checklist calls for BOTH guidance-mode switches at ATT HOLD.

steps.label: MODE CONT AGS
steps.instructions: The checklist calls for BOTH guidance-mode switches at ATT HOLD.

steps.label: TTCA CDR
steps.instructions: The checklist abbreviates this setting JET; the controller selector is JETS/THROTTLE.

steps.label: TTCA LMP
steps.instructions: The checklist abbreviates this setting JET; the controller selector is JETS/THROTTLE.

steps.label: ACA/4 JET CDR
steps.instructions: This is the separate 4-jet enable path; do not interpret DISABLE as all attitude control disabled.

steps.label: ACA/4 JET LMP
steps.instructions: This is the separate 4-jet enable path; do not interpret DISABLE as all attitude control disabled.

steps.label: Report the remaining preparation items checked
steps.instructions: Report rendezvous radar SLEW, AOT heater breaker closed, camera mounted, COAS installed, and circuit breakers verified against the original charts. These are crew reports.

steps.label: Report Columbia configured for undocking
steps.instructions: Report hand controllers adjusted/armed, THC power ON, GDC aligned and SCS/DAP/BMAG configuration checked using the flown Solo Book. CMC operations are not executed here.

steps.label: DOCK PROBE MNA circuit breaker
steps.locator: CMP Solo Book 66A; AOH docking system locator 3-47/3-48
steps.instructions: Both docking-probe circuit breakers are on CSM panel 8.

steps.label: DOCK PROBE MNB circuit breaker
steps.locator: CMP Solo Book 66A; AOH docking system locator 3-47/3-48
steps.instructions: Both docking-probe circuit breakers are on CSM panel 8.

steps.label: Report Eagle ready to Mike
steps.instructions: Confirm the LM checklist is ready before Collins operates the probe control. This represents the crew readiness exchange, not an AI-generated radio response.

steps.label: DOCKING PROBE - EXTD/REL
steps.instructions: Collins operates Columbia's probe extend/release control. In this discrete procedure model it releases the modeled connection. No probe timing, flight motion or sensor indication is simulated.

steps.label: DOCKING PROBE
steps.instructions: Return the control to OFF after the modeled release. Exact Apollo 11 hold duration is not established by the sources used here.

steps.label: Report separation visually confirmed
steps.instructions: Record a crew observation of release. The expanded 3D diagram shows the disconnected arrangement; it does not measure separation distance or velocity.

steps.label: Hand off to the inspection chapter
steps.instructions: Next came relative-motion management and LM inspection, then the separate CSM separation maneuver, LM alignment, DOI and P63 preparation. Do not skip directly to powered descent.

limitations: This is a playable selected procedure, not every Apollo 11 checklist item or a flight-qualified checklist replica.
Station assignment in the trainer routes controls to CDR, LMP or CMP; where the LM checklist does not identify a hand, the route is a teaching choice.
Control positions are modeled user selections. Crew reports acknowledge assumed tasks; they are not pressure, switch or latch sensor telemetry.
The release transition is a discrete training abstraction. There is no verified release duration, spring impulse, relative trajectory or achieved inspection attitude.
The two real probe indicators are contextual striped/gray flags, not a generic green undocked light; this trainer does not fabricate their readings.
Apollo 11 used the established release procedure. Do not substitute the later soft-undocking sequence that Armstrong described as untested before Apollo 11.
Further maneuvers remain unavailable until their actual guidance, controls and vehicle-state integration are implemented.
